items.claim: The row's confidence label sits above the calibration ceiling that applies to any row spanning a complete chapter.
items.evidence: web:Isa.6.1-web:Isa.6.13 covers the entirety of chapter 6 (13 of 13 verses); the governing calibration rule caps confidence at medium_low for a whole-chapter span regardless of internal seam strength, and this row is labeled high with no disclosed exception. The seam warrant and unit_type call are otherwise well grounded: a dated first-person vision onset at web:Isa.6.1 breaks from the preceding judgment scene, and the chapter boundary into a third-person narrative at web:Isa.7.1 closes it, so only the confidence label is at issue.

items.claim: The narrative frame plus embedded divine-speech reading of web:Isa.7.1-web:Isa.7.17, with the almah/Immanuel construal correctly held open, is well warranted.
items.evidence: Front seam: a fresh third-person narrative onset at web:Isa.7.1 breaks cleanly from the preceding first-person vision report. Rear seam: the mode shifts at web:Isa.7.18 from second-person address embedded in the narrative to third-person description of Yahweh's coming acts, a genuine frame-mode change rather than a bare topic label. The embedded koh-amar speech at web:Isa.7.7 is correctly kept inside its narrative frame per the frame-plus-speech default. The row neither names nor decides the almah/Immanuel referent at web:Isa.7.14, holding it open as required; confidence (medium_low) and an explicit frontier flag are appropriately set given the row touches the almah-sign hazard zone.
tier_citations: byte (direct source verification of web:Isa.7.1, web:Isa.7.7, web:Isa.7.14, web:Isa.7.18 wording)

items.claim: Keeping the four in-that-day images as one row rather than atomizing per onset is the correct application of the over-split-risk rule.
items.evidence: web:Isa.7.18, web:Isa.7.20, web:Isa.7.21, and web:Isa.7.23 share one addressee and one cumulative judgment image with no renewed divine-speech formula, hoy onset, or addressee shift between them, so no tier-1 marker licenses a finer cut. judgment_oracle is the correct operative default for announcement-of-judgment content outside the woe/massa frames. The disclosed rival (four-way atomization by onset) is the real alternative a writer would otherwise reach for, not a strawman.
tier_citations: tier-1 frame (absence of a renewed marker between the four sub-images)

items.claim: The Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz sign-act report is correctly isolated as its own vision_report unit.
items.evidence: Front seam: a fresh first-person divine-command onset at web:Isa.8.1 breaks from the preceding oracle cycle's impersonal form. Rear seam: the renewed formula at web:Isa.8.5 is an explicit divine-speech-frame renewal, distinct from a command-plus-fulfillment report. Sign-act reports including this one are grouped as vision_report, and the row's bounds match that classification.
tier_citations: tier-1 frame (divine-command onset; renewed speech formula)

items.claim: The Shiloah/Euphrates judgment oracle is correctly bounded at the renewed speech formula on the front and the vocative addressee shift to the nations on the back.
items.evidence: Front seam web:Isa.8.5 is a renewed divine-speech formula distinct from the preceding sign-act report. Rear seam web:Isa.8.9 opens with a plural vocative imperative summons to the nations, an explicit addressee shift recognized as tier-1. The row correctly holds the Immanuel-as-address construal at web:Isa.8.8 open rather than resolving it against the naming clause at web:Isa.7.14; confidence (medium_low) and a frontier flag are appropriately set given the row sits inside the Immanuel hazard zone.
tier_citations: tier-1 frame (renewed speech formula; vocative addressee shift)

items.claim: The two-verse taunt against the nations is correctly bounded by the vocative shift and correctly classified as judgment_oracle over the salvation_oracle rival.
items.evidence: The row opens on the same vocative addressee shift at web:Isa.8.9 that closes the preceding row, and closes before the renewed strong-hand formula at web:Isa.8.11 that opens a new divine word to Isaiah alone. The content is an announcement-of-doom form addressed to the nations, with the closing Immanuel clause read as theological ground rather than operative form, so judgment_oracle over salvation_oracle is a defensible operative-category call rather than a strawman rejection. Confidence and the frontier flag are appropriately hedged given the row falls inside the Immanuel hazard zone.
tier_citations: tier-1 frame (vocative addressee shift; renewed formula at close)

items.claim: The row's rear boundary at web:Isa.8.18 severs an undisclosed lexical inclusio that runs through web:Isa.8.20.
items.evidence: web:Isa.8.16's sealed-testimony command pairs the two terms torah and teudah (transliterated); the same two-term pairing recurs, order reversed, at web:Isa.8.20 -- a book-wide exclusive pairing (teudah occurs in only 2 verses in the whole book, both inside web:Isa.8.16 and web:Isa.8.20; torah occurs in 5 verses book-wide, with only this occurrence adjacent to a teudah site) that functions as an envelope bracketing the sealed-testimony material from web:Isa.8.16 through web:Isa.8.20. The row's own boundary at web:Isa.8.18 falls inside that bracket, and the recurrence is undisclosed in the row's own evidence; the bracket argues the unit runs at least through web:Isa.8.20 rather than closing at web:Isa.8.18.
tier_citations: byte (direct source verification of web:Isa.8.16, web:Isa.8.20 wording)
skeleton (book-wide exclusivity sweep: teudah 2 verses, torah 5 verses)

items.claim: The row's front boundary at web:Isa.8.19 rests on a bare topic-shift rationale that is not a recognized tier-1 frame marker, and it opens inside an undisclosed lexical bracket spanning web:Isa.8.16-web:Isa.8.20.
items.evidence: web:Isa.8.19 opens with a plain conditional continuation clause introduced by a coordinating waw, not a hoy onset, massa header, renewed speech formula, or vocative addressee shift; the row's stated seam rationale is a bare topic label, which the granularity rule treats as insufficient absent a tier-1 marker at the cut. The torah/teudah pairing (transliterated; book-wide exclusive per a skeleton sweep: teudah 2 verses, torah 5 verses) recurs at web:Isa.8.16 and web:Isa.8.20, bracketing material that spans across this row's own front boundary; the row's evidence does not disclose the recurrence, and the bracket argues the row's true front seam sits after web:Isa.8.20, not before web:Isa.8.19.
tier_citations: tier-1 frame (absence of a recognized marker at web:Isa.8.19)
byte (direct source verification of web:Isa.8.16, web:Isa.8.20 wording)
